artworks.title: Madame Cezanne
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows a sketch of a person's head and partial neck in profile, facing right. The facial features include a nose, mouth, and chin. The hair is styled with curved lines and extends to the nape of the neck. The sketch features minimalistic details, with a line indicating a collar. There are no additional elements in the blank background.

artworks.title: Study of a Decorative Ornament
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image displays an arrangement of swirling lines and curved shapes forming an abstract design. The composition features ornate, flowing patterns that resemble stylized clouds or ocean waves. The undulating forms and layered lines create an intricate pattern that moves the eye across the page in a dynamic, sweeping motion, akin to decorative elements in classical art or architecture.

artworks.title: Madame Cezanne
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image depicts a sketched drawing of a person's head and partial upper torso. The head is in a three-quarter view, with loosely defined facial features such as the eyes, nose, and mouth. The hair is textured with lines suggesting volume. The individual seems to be wearing a garment with a collar, and the background is a plain, light-colored surface. There are no visible accessories or additional objects.

artworks.title: Study of the Allegorical Figure of Health in Rubens' "The Birth of Louis XIII"
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image is a sketch of a human figure showing the torso and arm. The person appears to be lying down, with the head slightly turned to the side. The drawing emphasizes the muscular contours of the arm and torso with light pencil strokes. The head and facial features are minimally depicted. There are no visible clothing details or objects in the person's hand. The background consists of the blank page the sketch is drawn on, which is part of an open sketchbook.

artworks.title: Two Heads of Women
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows a pencil sketch of two heads, focusing on their facial features and hair. Both individuals are depicted in a three-quarter view from above, with their heads angled downward. The person on the left has gathered hair, closed eyes, and a serene expression. The person on the right has hair styled similarly, with closed eyes and a similar downward angle to their face. The sketch is drawn on textured paper, with a slightly visible binding on the left edge. There are no visible clothing details or background elements in the image, which focuses on the faces and hair.

artworks.title: Woman Leaning Forward
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows a sketch of a person, depicting only the upper part of their body - the head and a partial view of the upper torso. The person is lying down with their face tilted slightly upwards and turned to the side, appearing calm. Their eyes are closed, and they have short to medium-length hair styled or combed backward. The sketch does not include details about clothing, jewelry or objects. The background is a textured pencil shading that creates a soft, indistinct environment, emphasizing the person's peaceful facial expression.

artworks.title: Woman Leaning Forward
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image is a top-down sketch of a person's head showing facial features and hair styled in a bun or updo. The sketch captures the top part of the head, facial structure, eyes, and nose. The rest of the body is not detailed, with a hint of the neck and shoulder. The background is a shaded graphite texture.

artworks.title: Bellows in Front of a Fireplace
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The sketch shows a large folded umbrella with a handle positioned diagonally across the center of the page. The color palette consists of pencil shades of gray. In the background are loosely sketched shapes resembling an apple and other indistinct objects. The handle is pointed upwards and slightly to the right, while the fabric of the umbrella drapes downwards towards the bottom left corner of the page.

artworks.title: Fireplace Tongs and Poker
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows a detailed pencil sketch of a trumpet. The trumpet extends from the left side towards the center of the page, with its rounded bell ending near the middle, while the mouthpiece and several valves are visible in the foreground. The sketch is done in gray and black hues. The rest of the page is blank.

artworks.title: Cushion of an Armchair
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image displays an arrangement of curved pencil lines that create movement and organic shapes. The central element swirls like a spiral, resembling a seashell or a chameleon's tail. The composition evokes natural forms without depicting a specific object, suggesting shapes commonly seen in nature.

artworks.title: Madame Cezanne with her Head Lowered
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The drawing shows a person's head and part of the neck in a reclining position. The face is slightly tilted upwards and to the side, with delicately highlighted facial features including the curvature of the head, the nasal profile, and closed eyes. The short, slightly wavy hair follows the contour of the head. The off-white paper contains two notations, one with the number "33" in the upper right corner and the other marked "XVII" at the bottom right. The background is plain, keeping the focus on the sketched figure.

artworks.title: The Artist's Son Writing
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: Drawn with delicate, overlapping lines and bold, parallel lines for shading in graphite on beige-colored paper, a person hunches over a surface and writes with one hand. The person’s head, hulking shoulders, hands, and the paper on which he writes fill most of the composition. His face is close to the page, and his head tips to our right. Shading suggests eyelashes, nose, ear, and jawline. The background is blank, and the edges of the page and sketchbook are visible.

artworks.title: The Artist's Son
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image is a pencil sketch of a person in profile view from the shoulders up. The person has a gentle expression with a closed eye and a hint of a nose. The person's short, neatly combed hair is visible. The sketch includes the shoulders and a simple garment. The background is plain white sketch paper.

artworks.title: Head of a Boy
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image is a sketch depicting a close-up view of a person's face, primarily showing the head and neck. The person is facing slightly downward to the left. Their facial features are delicately rendered, with closed eyes and a slightly pursed mouth. The hair is short and appears to be combed backward, adding definition to the head's silhouette. The person is dressed in a simple garment, likely a shirt, suggested by soft lines indicating the collar. There is no noticeable jewelry or objects in hand, but a loosely outlined hand sketch appears on the left side. The background is blank, which emphasizes the sketch's focus on the subject's face and expression.

artworks.title: Head of a Boy Seen from Behind
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: This image depicts a detailed pencil sketch of a person's head and neck from a side view. The sketch showcases the back of the ear, the curve of the neck, and varying light and shadow angles. The background is plain with no other elements. The image is on a page with a visible binding on the left side and the number "37" in the top right corner. The sketch employs pencil shading with different line densities to illustrate the skin's contours and texture.

artworks.title: Carnival Scene
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image displays a series of flowing, intertwining lines and shapes forming an abstract composition. The forms curve and twist, resembling human figures in dynamic poses. The sketchy quality and overlapping strokes suggest movement, like a dance or struggle. The abstract drawing prompts the viewer to interpret the relationships and positions of the forms, potentially evoking images of intertwined or embracing figures.

artworks.title: Woman Leaning Forward
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows a pencil sketch of a person's upper body, emphasizing the head and shoulders. The person is depicted with their head leaning forward. The sketch outlines the person's head, short hair or a closely cropped style, and some facial features partly hidden. The clothing is plain, suggesting a collared garment. There are no visible accessories. The background is plain, and there are handwritten inscriptions on the right side naming "Antonio Franchi" and dated "der März 1911."

artworks.title: Head of the Artist's Son
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows a pencil sketch of a person's head in profile. Only the upper part of the head is visible, from above the ear to the jawline. The person appears to be lying down with their head slightly tilted. The drawing captures the general outline of the face, focusing on the ear and the shading of the cheek and jawline. The hair is depicted with short, straight strokes suggesting a short haircut. There is no depiction of the person's clothing or any objects. The background is a blank page. The drawing is on an open page of a sketchbook, evident from the visible binding and adjacent blank pages on both sides.

artworks.title: Branch in Flower
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a stylized, abstract form with flowing lines and intricate details. The drawing features a series of curved lines suggesting a floral or organic motif, emanating from the left side of the paper. The central portion of the drawing includes a series of overlapping lines that may represent leaves or petals, creating a sense of motion and complexity. The background is blank, allowing the focus to remain on the design on the left. The simplicity of the background and the detailed line work suggest a study or exploration of form and movement, capturing the graceful, organic nature of its thematic elements.

artworks.title: Pine Tree
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image shows a sketch of what seems to be a tree or branch structure. The drawing is done from a close, slightly elevated perspective, focusing on intricate details of the subject. There is no clear horizon visible in the sketch. The artist uses loose, flowing lines and shading to create depth and form. Areas of denser cross-hatching are used to depict shadows. The color palette is monochrome, with shades of gray and black created by pencil on light paper, giving the sketch a raw, unfinished look.

artworks.title: Women Bathers and a Roll of Paper
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image is a drawing of abstract forms and sketchy lines on paper. The left side features lines resembling a face, while the right side has curved marks suggesting movement and fluidity. The drawing has a spontaneous and exploratory style, with freehand lines demonstrating creativity.

artworks.title: Hand and Shoulder of a Boy
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image features a sketch of a partial figure, mainly showing the hands and part of the head. The body is mostly hidden, with a focus on the hands clasped near the face. The head is slightly tilted forward, with hair suggested by soft pencil strokes. Facial features are not detailed, providing an impressionistic representation. The sketch lacks defined clothing or surroundings, emphasizing the hands and head outline. The background is plain, with light shading around the figure's shoulders or back. The sketch is done in pencil on off-white paper, likely from a sketchbook.

artworks.title: Two Heads
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image features a sketch of two individuals viewed primarily from their shoulders up. The person on the left is depicted in a profile position with slight chin lowered and one visible eye. They appear to have short hair. The individual on the right is also shown in profile with a detailed facial structure, including outlined nose and lips. This person has wavy hair falling slightly over their forehead. Both individuals are drawn in a minimalist style using careful pencil strokes. No clothing details or jewelry are included, and both figures appear to be wearing some form of garment. The background is plain, emphasizing the focus on the sketches of the two individuals.

artworks.title: Study of Puget's "Hercules Resting"
artworks.creditLine: Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
artworks.description: The image is a sketch of an individual shown from the back, with the upper body prominently displayed. The person is seated, facing away from the viewer, creating a profile view of the left side of their face and part of their torso. The person's facial features are minimally detailed, with simple lines indicating the nose and basic shape of the face, while the hair is suggested with loose, flowing lines showing it as short and slightly wavy. There is no visible clothing on the person, and the focus is on the contours and musculature of the back, arms, and part of the side. The sketch is drawn on a plain page, with the background left mostly blank. The page number '47' is visible in the upper right corner of the open book where the sketch appears.
